name: Tim Rose-Richards
features: fair skin, dark hair slicked back from a high forehead, light eyes, long narrow face, prominent ears, tall slight build, shy amused smile
bio: Thomas Essery Rose-Richards, a Welsh stockbroker who raced for the fun of it and was better at it than that suggests. Third overall at Le Mans three years running — Talbot AV105 in 1931 and 1932, Alfa Romeo 8C 2300 in 1933 — and third in the 1933 Tourist Trophy. He shared John Cobb's Napier-Railton to win the 1935 Brooklands 500 and take a BRDC Gold Star, and set 24-hour records with him at Bonneville. Flying a Fleet Air Arm Walrus to pick up a downed Luftwaffe pilot off Anvil Point in October 1940, he was shot down by two Heinkel 111s and killed.
